title.narrative: Ukuthula Trust: Navigating a Path to Reviving Democracy in Zimbabwe 2021 - 2024
Ukuthula Trust: Navigating a Path to Reviving Democracy in Zimbabwe 2021 - 2024

description.narrative:
The Ukuthula Trust seeks to achieve these broader objectives through the following objectives:
Project Goal: To deepen democracy by empowering people to release their energy towards taking an active part in the development and governance of their communities, through rehabilitation of communities and through prevention of conflict in Zimbabwe in the future by generating knowledge and promoting accountability.
1. Ukuthula Trust försöker uppnå dessa bredare mål genom följande:
Projektmål: Att fördjupa demokratin genom att ge människor möjlighet att aktivt ta del i utvecklingen och styrningen av sina samhällen, genom rehabilitering av samhällen, och genom att förebygga framtida konflikter i Zimbabwe genom att generera kunskap och främja ansvarsskyldighet. 1.Fördjupad demokrati: Att stärka och främja fattiga och marginaliserade samhällen, med särskilt fokus på kvinnor och ungdomar, i ett försök att öka den lokala och nationella regeringens öppenhet, ansvarsskyldighet och lyhördhet för dessa samhällen.
2.Återställa social struktur och rehabilitera offer för kollektivt våld: Att förbättra samhällets sammanhållning, inklusive kvinnor och ungdomar, så att alla medlemmar i samhället aktivt kan delta i utvecklingen.
3.Skapa kunskap: Att aktivt främja omprövning av begrepp kopplade till demokrati, ungdom, kön, utveckling och historiskt våld i Zimbabwe.
4.Lobbying och påverkansarbete: Att främja och påverka politiska förändringar i Zimbabwe.

Over the past four years, Ukuthula Trust has consistently demonstrated its commitment to empowering communities. Beginning with initiatives focused on skills development, the organization expanded its efforts to include livelihood creation and later strengthened inclusive governance practices. This sustained approach has resulted in tangible outcomes that improved lives and enhanced resilience across multiple sectors. Due to the sensitive nature of certain activities, the cooperation partner chose not to disclose specific details in formal reports. However, evidence of the partners ability to learn and adapt was shared with Sida during meetings and field visits.
Skills Development and Economic Empowerment: During the reporting period, 304 students graduated from the Enyandeni and Enqameni centres, acquiring practical skills in sewing, brick-laying, food preparation, hairdressing, welding, hair braiding, and computer literacy. These achievements have not only created new income-generating opportunities but also enhanced household economic resilience, enabling families to break cycles of poverty. Strategic partnerships amplified these efforts. Mtshabezi High School donated five desktop computers to Enyandeni, while Blanket Mine provided five laptops to Enqameni, expanding access to digital training and bridging the technology gap. The Enyandeni Garden Project further demonstrated sustainable success, with a dedicated team cultivating and selling vegetables, reinvesting profits into inputs, and improving techniques through collaboration with Agritex officers. This initiative boosted household incomes and improved food security, showcasing the power of community-driven enterprise.
Inclusive Governance and Community Engagement: Ukuthula Trusts approach remained firmly rooted in community engagement and participatory governance. By working closely with traditional leaders, development committees, faith groups, Members of Parliament, and local authorities, the Trust ensured interventions were locally relevant, community-owned, and aligned with governance structures. This inclusive model fostered trust, accountability, and shared responsibility, laying the foundation for long-term development.
Healing and Justice for Gukurahundi Survivors: A cornerstone of Ukuthulas work has been its unwavering support for Gukurahundi survivors, particularly women affected by sexual violence. Through community sensitization meetings and targeted group sessions, survivors were provided with safe spaces for healing and dialogue, enabling them to share experiences and articulate expectations for reparations in an environment rooted in empathy and dignity. These efforts, carried out in collaboration with traditional leaders, delivered psychosocial support to 1,822 survivors, with 128 receiving specialized assistance.
Testimonies revealed recurring traumatic experiences forced disappearances, mass graves, sexual violence leading to unwanted pregnancies, family conflicts, and coerced participation in prolonged night meetings. In response, Ukuthula actively engaged in institutional collaboration and advocacy, advising the Gukurahundi Steering Committee and supporting the Ministry of Justice in strengthening the Community Outreach Programme. Although village-level hearings had not yet commenced, Ukuthula ensured adherence to the do no harm principle, safeguarding survivor dignity.
Forensic Anthropology and Cultural Closure: Beyond psychosocial support, Ukuthulas Forensic Anthropology Team partnered with local chiefs to conduct exhumations and reburials, offering cultural closure and reinforcing the right to remembrance and justice. In 2024 alone, the team carried out three major exhumations, including a mass grave and a deeply symbolic recovery in Tsholotsho, which reunited a son with his fathers remains after decades of separation. These efforts underscored the humanizing role of forensic science in restoring dignity, rebuilding family ties, and preserving historical memory. Collaborations with United Bulawayo Hospitals further strengthened national forensic capacity, enabling identification of victims from mining accidents and other unresolved cases.
Thought Leadership and Regional Dialogue: Ukuthula also cemented its role as a thought leader through its annual Critical Thinking Workshop, held in Sandton, South Africa. This platform convened civic leaders, activists, and academics from Zimbabwe, South Africa, and Zambia, fostering regional dialogue on civil society challenges and strategies. Insights generated from these engagements informed advocacy at local, national, and international levels, shaping policy and reinforcing Ukuthulas commitment to healing, justice, and participatory governance.
